column1: # Actor head table: which head words name an actor, and their broad class.
# Each line: <word ending> TAB <class>. A head word belongs to a class when its
# plain form (lowercase, no accents, no hyphens) ends with the ending; the
# longest matching ending wins. So one line covers compounds too:
# Regular plurals (-s, -en, -n) are found without a line of their own;
# plurals with a changed vowel ('lidstaten', 'organen') need one.
# Class '-' marks words that end like an actor but are not one.
#   institution  EU or national institution, court
#   body         committee, office, agency or other body
#   office       a post or the members/staff of a body
#   party        a party the rules apply to: provider, controller, undertaking
#   person       a natural or legal person, the persons affected
# not actors, although they end like one
